context: Delete benchbox/cli/execution_pipeline.py and its three test files. Update docs/design/structure.md:189, docs/development/runtime-modules.md:16, and docs/development/run-lifecycle-map.md:18,41-42 which reference it. Confirm no dynamic/string-based import exists before deleting.
description: benchbox/cli/execution_pipeline.py (430 lines) has zero production importers. Its only importers are three test files that test the module itself: tests/unit/cli/test_execution_pipeline.py (306 lines), tests/unit/cli/test_execution_pipeline_driver_metadata.py (106), tests/unit/cli/test_cli_benchmark_boundaries.py (27). The repo already documents it as non-runtime: docs/development/runtime-modules.md:16 calls it a 'legacy compatibility/test module; not the default benchbox run runtime path' and docs/design/structure.md:189 agrees. It is absent from docs/reference/public-contracts.md. Its four stages now map one-to-one onto responsibilities benchbox/core/run_service.py owns: ConfigurationValidationStage->resolve_run_config, BenchmarkLoadingStage->core.benchmark_loader, PlatformAdapterStage->the injected adapter_factory, BenchmarkExecutionStage->execute_run, and _enrich_driver_metadata->the shared apply_driver_metadata helper. Discovered while scoping one-engine-core-run-service w4, whose unit text says 'CLI orchestrator/execution_pipeline migrate onto the service; delete moved code' -- migrating this module into core would wire dead code into the layer the program is trying to keep clean, so deletion is the correct disposition. Split out of w4 to honor the keystone anti-pattern that improvements ship separately from extractions, matching the precedent set by one-engine-delete-dead-mcp and one-engine-residual-dedup.

preserves.behavior: Driver-metadata enrichment continues to flow through the shared apply_driver_metadata helper in core, not the deleted ExecutionEngine method.
No production code path changes: the module has no non-test importers, so deletion must not alter benchbox run behavior.
